chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
When you face the qiblah with your face, then do not turn your face away from the qiblah, lest you invalidate your salat.
For Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the obligatory prayer: “So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.”
And be humble with your gaze, and do not raise it toward the sky; rather, keep it level with your face at the place of your sajdah.

key_terms.شَطْرَ: toward or in the direction of
key_terms.صَلَاتَكَ: your salat, the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ: the place where you perform sajdah
key_terms.وَاخْشَعْ: show humility and attentiveness in prayer

ai.seo_question: Does turning your face away from the qiblah invalidate salat?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the worshipper to remain facing the qiblah during salat and warns that turning the face away invalidates the prayer. It also teaches khushu' in prayer by lowering the gaze toward the place of sajdah, grounding the ruling in the Quranic command to face al-Masjid al-Haram.
